note: Rodent fibrosis and metabolic models predicted the biomarker wins (ALT, liver fat, rat fibrosis) but were silent on pruritus and predicted the wrong direction for LDL; only obeticholic acid carried fibrosis into patients.
label: MASH (FXR agonists)

engagement.note: 6-ECDCA (obeticholic acid) drove the FXR-SHP cascade in rat liver and stellate cells; no patient read-out yet.
engagement.short: OCA induced SHP in rat liver
engagement.quote: Exposure of HSCs to FXR ligands caused a 3-fold increase of SHP, reduced alpha1(I)collagen and TGF-beta1 by approximately 60%-70% and abrogates alpha1(I) collagen mRNA up-regulation induced by thrombin and TGF-beta1.

engagement.model: Rodent FXR target-gene pharmacodynamics (SHP, Fgf15, Cyp7a1)
engagement.note: Obeticholic acid 25/50 mg raised FGF19 and lowered C4 and bile acids in NAFLD patients, the rodent FXR signature.
engagement.short: FGF19 up, C4 down in patients
engagement.quote: They also had increased serum levels of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and fibroblast growth factor 19, associated with decreased levels of 7α-hydroxy-4-cholesten-3-one and endogenous bile acids, indicating activation of farnesoid X receptor.
engagement.confidence: medium (abstract only, paywalled; the rodent-vs-human PD juxtaposition is ours; cohort was T2D + NAFLD, not biopsy-confirmed MASH)
engagement.judgement: Juxtaposed: rodent FXR-SHP/Fgf15/Cyp7a1 induction (Fiorucci 2004; Tully 2017 rodent PD, doi:10.1021/acs.jmedchem.7b00907) against the human FGF19/C4 signature; no source states the cross-species comparison. Mudaliar's cohort was T2D + NAFLD rather than biopsy-confirmed MASH; the same markers moved in cilofexor's NASH phase 2 (Patel 2020, doi:10.1002/hep.31205: C4 and primary bile acids fell) and tropifexor gave dose-dependent FGF19 rises in healthy volunteers (Badman 2020, doi:10.1002/cpdd.762).

dose.note: Rat antifibrotic doses were 1-10 mg/kg; no published rodent-to-human exposure comparison, and clinical doses were capped by pruritus.
dose.short: Rat doses never mapped to patients
dose.quote: Twelve-week administration of 1-10 mg/kg 6-ethyl chenodeoxycholic acid (6-ECDCA), a synthetic FXR ligand, to porcine serum-treated rats prevented liver fibrosis development and reduced liver expression of alpha1(I) collagen, TGF-beta1 and alpha-SMA mRNA by approximately 90%.
dose.judgement: Looked for a published rodent-exposure-to-human-dose comparison (OCA 25 mg vs 3-30 mg/kg in rats/mice; tropifexor 140-200 µg vs <1 mg/kg in STAM/AMLN mice, Hernandez 2019) and found none; the FDA NASH review that would carry exposure multiples was never published (complete response letters 2020 and 2023). Human doses were set by pruritus tolerability, not by a model exposure target.

efficacy.note: Obeticholic acid (6-ECDCA) cut fibrosis and collagen/TGF-β1 mRNA 70-80% in bile-duct-ligated rats; later Zucker rats and DIO mice added steatosis.
efficacy.quote: Therapeutic administration of 6-ECDCA, 3 mg/kg, to BDL rats reduced liver fibrosis and alpha1(I) collagen, transforming growth factor (TGF)-beta1, alpha-SMA, and tissue metalloproteinase inhibitor (TIMP)-1 and 2 messenger RNA (mRNA) by 70%-80%.

efficacy.note: FLINT: obeticholic acid 25 mg improved NAS in 45% vs 21% and fibrosis in 35% vs 19%, as rat models predicted.
efficacy.quote: Importantly, all components of the NAFLD activity score (steatosis, hepatocellular ballooning, and lobular inflammation) and fibrosis improved.
efficacy.confidence: high (open-access author manuscript PMC4447192 read in full)
efficacy.judgement: The FLINT paper itself frames the animal prediction ('reduces liver fat and fibrosis in animal models of fatty liver disease') against the patient result, so comparison_stated is true at direction level; the 35% vs 19% fibrosis figure is FLINT's, as quoted by Hernandez 2019. REGENERATE (Younossi 2019, doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(19)33041-7; NCT02548351 results posted 2024-09-05) repeated the match: fibrosis improvement 23% vs 12% at 25 mg, NASH resolution not met. Tølbøl 2018 (doi:10.3748/wjg.v24.i2.179) later found OCA did not reduce fibrosis in biopsy-confirmed DIO-NASH/ob/ob-NASH mice yet called those models 'in general agreement' with FLINT; not entered because they were not the model OCA relied on. FLINT required biopsy-confirmed NASH but not fibrosis.

efficacy.note: Tropifexor reversed established fibrosis in STAM and AMLN mice; FLIGHT-FXR found no fibrosis or NASH-resolution gain over placebo at 48 weeks.
efficacy.short: Tropifexor: mouse fibrosis reversal, no patient gain
efficacy.quote: Despite improvement in biomarkers of liver injury and indirect indicators of histologic improvement after 48 weeks of tropifexor treatment, greater histologic improvement of fibrosis or resolution of NASH relative to placebo was not observed
efficacy.confidence: medium (full text PMC9941046 read; quote is the first 34 words of a 46-word sentence that ends 'based on the central pathologist's assessment using the traditional semiquantitative NASH CRN scoring system'; contra is a judgement call, see judgement)
efficacy.judgement: Contra rests on tropifexor: Novartis's own STAM/AMLN work (Hernandez 2019, doi:10.1002/hep4.1368: 'tropifexor reversed established fibrosis') versus ≥1-stage fibrosis improvement 26%/26% vs 21% placebo, with the trial paper's own 'treatment efficacy in animal models of NASH' framing (comparison_stated true). Caveats the authors raise: 48-week duration, histology a secondary endpoint, pruritus-capped doses, and digital qFibrosis (Sanyal 2022, doi:10.1016/j.jhep.2022.06.018) showed dose-dependent regression. Cilofexor monotherapy also missed fibrosis in ATLAS (Loomba 2021, doi:10.1002/hep.31622: 12% vs 11%; NCT03449446 results posted 2020-12-03) but its sponsor model is unpublished (the rat model is academic: Schwabl 2021, doi:10.3390/biomedicines9010060), so 2021 was not used as the contra year. EDP-305 (ARGON-1, Ratziu 2022, doi:10.1016/j.jhep.2021.10.018) and vonafexor (LIVIFY, Ratziu 2023, doi:10.1016/j.jhep.2022.10.023) have only ALT/liver-fat read-outs.

safety.note: FXR agonism lowered triglycerides and VLDL in mice; obeticholic acid 'corrected lipid abnormalities' in Zucker rats; rodents cannot report itch.
safety.quote: Cholic acid (CA) prevents hepatic TG accumulation, VLDL secretion, and elevated serum TG in mouse models of hypertriglyceridemia.

safety.note: FLINT: pruritus 23% vs 6% and LDL rose; rodents predicted lipid lowering and atherosclerosis regression and could not flag itch.
safety.short: Pruritus 23%, LDL up; mice said down
safety.quote: The positive findings are tempered by the observation of pruritus in 23% of patients and an increase in total cholesterol and LDL cholesterol, and a modest decrease in HDL cholesterol.
safety.confidence: high (open-access author manuscript PMC4447192 read in full)
safety.reason: Missed pruritus; LDL rose, rodents predicted fall
safety.judgement: The FLINT discussion itself sets 'In animal models, farnesoid X receptor agonists cause regression of atherosclerosis' against the atherogenic lipid shift in patients, so comparison_stated is true; the HDL fall was in fact foreshadowed in Zucker rats (Cipriani 2010, doi:10.1194/jlr.M001602). LDL rise had already appeared in NAFLD/T2D patients (Mudaliar 2013) and in healthy volunteers (Pencek 2016, doi:10.1111/dom.12681). Papazyan 2018 (doi:10.1194/jlr.M081935) later stated the species split outright ('FXR activation induces distinct changes in circulating cholesterol among animal models and humans') and showed humanized-liver chimeric mice reproduce the LDL rise; a re-scorer requiring a stated mouse-vs-human comparison could date this entry 2018. Pruritus proved a class effect no rodent model flagged: REGENERATE 51% at 25 mg, EDP-305 50.9% at 2.5 mg (Ratziu 2022), tropifexor 52-69% (Sanyal 2023), cilofexor 14% (Patel 2020), vonafexor 18% (Ratziu 2023); Hernandez 2019 predicted a GPBAR1-sparing non-bile-acid agonist would 'reduce side effects', which FLIGHT-FXR falsified.
